title: Template Authoring
body:
This Signature record covers Template Authoring within the Workflow Templates and Playbooks Signature Database. Reusable procedures for complex, multi-stage jobs. It is Manon's original design for this topic, written for the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source.

How it works. Template method: a tested multi-stage procedure is parameterized for the job at hand, with gates, rollback steps, and an audit trail. The Signature version keeps the same honest structure as the public record: stated inputs, a repeatable procedure, stated outputs, and explicit limits. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the simple rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Signature framing. Manon's original Signature playbook designs: reusable multi-stage procedures inside the Signature ecosystem.

Scope and limits. This record describes Manon's original designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how template authoring is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.

# Template Authoring: playbook stage timing
steps = [4, 6, 3, 5, 2]

title: Template Migration
body:
This Signature record covers Template Migration within the Workflow Templates and Playbooks Signature Database. Reusable procedures for complex, multi-stage jobs. It is Manon's original design for this topic, written for the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source.

How it works. Template method: a tested multi-stage procedure is parameterized for the job at hand, with gates, rollback steps, and an audit trail. The Signature version keeps the same honest structure as the public record: stated inputs, a repeatable procedure, stated outputs, and explicit limits. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.

Teaching ladder. This record sits at the most-complex rung: simple records introduce one idea cleanly, compounded records combine ideas, and most-complex records carry the whole chain with its failure modes and verification steps.

Signature framing. Manon's original Signature playbook designs: reusable multi-stage procedures inside the Signature ecosystem.

Scope and limits. This record describes Manon's original designs; it does not claim a live deployment, a vendor product, or an agency endorsement. Where a design is speculative it is labeled as a design, and the demo shows the calculation rather than a deployed system.

Further detail. This record also notes how template migration is reviewed over time: the method is re-checked against new examples, its limits are re-stated when the inputs change, and its demo is re-run whenever the record is revised, so the stored output always matches the stored code.
demo_code:
# Template Migration: playbook stage timing
steps = [4, 7, 3, 5, 2]
print('stages:', len(steps))
print('total_minutes:', sum(steps))
print('longest_stage:', max(steps))
